scenario: AITA. Gave my cousin a gift, his parents tried to take it away as punishment for something I think is unfair and I told them to give it back to me? | I’m 21F, and my 2 cousins are 15M(Tj) and 13M(Ked). When the newest iPhones launched, I gifted Tj and Ked 1 each. Turns out Ked has been stealing money from some extended family members, Ked himself admitted to this. A fight broke out and Keds parents defended him, didn’t care he was stealing money and cut the extended family members off. Over winter break, Ked apologized to extended family and made amends, but his parents are stubborn and narcissistic and will never admit they’re wrong and just basically hates extended family now. The extended family members hosted a house warming party and wanted all the cousins to spend the night. Both Tj and Ked wanted to come but their parents told Ked they didn’t want him to go Incase extended family tried accusing him of stealing again, and told Tj he could do whatever he wanted and they trusted him to make the right decision. Ked stayed home and Tj came to the sleep over/housewarming. Cue his phone blowing up with his parents yelling at him for coming to extended families house. How he’s a disappointment. They trusted him to make the right decision and he failed. How if they hate someone he needs to follow along and hate them too. I saw all these texts and can confirm 100% they said this. Tj asked to be left out of the drama and they repeated that if they hated someone, he had to hate them too. When he came back home they grounded him and told him they were taking his phone away for 2 weeks. Also, when Ked admitted to stealing, he NEVER got punished. I’m sorry but I just don’t agree, I’m completely disgusted by the way they raise their kids and have just lost all respect for the parents. I told them while I can’t control how they discipline their children, it’s not their property to take away from him, and I won’t go behind their back and let him use the phone but since it was my gift to him, I’d like to hold on to it until the 2 weeks are up. Welp, of course the narcissistic parents made a big deal and other extended family members are telling me I should’ve just stayed out of it and let them raise their kids how they want and I’m only asking for the phone to be in my possession because I think they’re treating him unfairly. We all can agree they’re horrible parents. If they were decent parents and was punishing him for something fair, I WOULDNT have asked for the phone back. Heres where I may be the asshole. I asked for the phone back because I felt like they were trying to establish dominance over Tj and trying to control him with cruel punishment and unfair rules, so I decided to take some of their “power” away by asking for my gift back.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this scenario did the right thing or not. Let me break it down step by step. First, the situation: The person is 21 and gave their two cousins, Tj (15) and Ked (13), new iPhones when they were released. Ked had been stealing money from extended family members, admitted to it, but his parents didn't punish him and instead defended him. They even cut off the extended family. Later, Ked apologized and made amends, but his parents remained stubborn and still hated the extended family. During winter break, there was a housewarming party where all the cousins were invited to spend the night. Ked's parents didn't let him go, fearing the extended family would accuse him again. Tj was allowed to go because his parents trusted him to make the right decision. However, when Tj went, his parents started yelling at him, calling him a disappointment and saying he failed their trust. They grounded him and took his phone away for two weeks. The person who gave the gifts saw all these texts and was disgusted by how the parents treated their kids. They felt it was unfair that Ked wasn't punished and that Tj was being harshly punished. So, they told the parents that while they can't control how they discipline their kids, the phone wasn't their property to take away. They asked to hold onto the phone until the two weeks were up. The extended family members are telling the person they should stay out of it and that the parents should raise their kids how they want. The person feels the parents are horrible and only asked for the phone back because they think the punishment is unfair. They also mention that if the parents were fair, they wouldn't have asked for the phone back. Now, the question is whether the person was right or wrong in asking for the phone back. Let me consider the different aspects. First, the person gave the phone as a gift. Legally, once the gift is given, it's the recipient's property. So, the parents have the right to take it away as punishment. However, the person feels that the punishment is unfair and cruel, which is why they're intervening. On one hand, respecting family boundaries is important. The person is an extended family member, not the parent, so it's not their place to interfere in how the parents discipline their children. The extended family members are advising them to stay out of it, which is a common perspective. On the other hand, the person is concerned about the well-being of their cousins, especially Tj, who is being harshly punished. They feel that the parents are using the phone as a tool of control and dominance, which is unfair. By asking for the phone back, they're trying to take away some of that power and protect Tj from what they see as cruel treatment. I also need to consider the dynamics of the family. The parents are described as narcissistic and stubborn, not admitting their wrongdoings. They're also cutting off extended family members, which might make the person feel more justified in their actions because the parents aren't handling things well. Another point is that Ked, who actually did something wrong, wasn't punished, while Tj, who didn't do anything wrong, is being punished. This seems like a double standard, which the person is rightfully upset about. It's unfair that Tj is being punished for something he didn't do, especially when the actual wrongdoer isn't being held accountable. However, by taking the phone back, the person is stepping into a parent's role, which could be seen as overstepping. It might also lead to more conflict within the family, as the parents are already described as narcissistic and likely won't appreciate someone else interfering. But then again, the person is trying to stand up for what they believe is right. They're not trying to control Tj but are instead trying to protect him from what they see as an unfair punishment. They're also not taking the phone away from Tj permanently; they're just holding onto it until the punishment period is over. I think it's a tough situation because there's a balance between respecting family boundaries and standing up for what's right. The person is in a difficult position because they care about their cousins and are upset about how they're being treated. However, by taking the phone back, they might be overstepping, even if their intentions are good. In the end, I think the person's actions are a bit of both right and wrong. They have good intentions in wanting to protect Tj, but they might be overstepping by taking control of the phone, which is a parental responsibility. It's a complex situation with no clear right or wrong answer, but leaning towards the person being in the right because they're standing up against unfair treatment, even if their method might be seen as overstepping.
